title.value: Environmental Risk of Psychiatric Disease: A Systematic Review on Air Pollution, Mental Health, and Frontolimbic Brain Regions
title.justification: The title explicitly mentions the environmental risk of psychiatric disease, focusing on air pollution and its effects on mental health and brain regions.
title.quote: P395. Environmental Risk of Psychiatric Disease: A Systematic Review on Air Pollution, Mental Health, and Frontolimbic Brain Regions

extractions.description: This paper systematically reviews existing literature on the effects of air pollution on mental health, particularly in relation to anxiety and depressive disorders. It investigates the association between air pollutants and structural/functional changes in brain regions such as the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, which are implicated in psychopathology.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper's focus is on the environmental impact of air pollution, a significant aspect of ecological health.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: The harmful effects of air pollution on respiratory and cardiovascular health are well established, however, its effects on mental health are less clear.

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on air pollution and its effects on mental health and cognitive functions.
primary_category.quote: This review identified that: 1) more studies are needed examining neural consequences of air pollution in humans, and 2) animal studies need to clearly define the age of animals at exposure so that translational windows of susceptibility may be identified.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not prominently address other sustainable development categories besides air pollution.

primary_sub_category.justification: The specific focus on air pollution and its link to mental health and structural brain changes makes it fit squarely within the air pollution sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: Air pollutants most examined were particulates (PM2.5 - 68%, multiple particulates e 17%, UFP e 14%, PM10 e 1%).

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No other sub-category under Pollution or other categories was evident in the paper's focus.

applications.value: Study of air pollution's impact on mental health
applications.justification: The paper systematically reviews the impact of air pollution on mental health, providing an application in terms of environmental health science.
applications.quote: Seventy-five percent and 66% of studies reported higher depressive and anxiety symptoms, respectively, with higher air pollution exposure.

applications.value: Investigating structural brain changes due to air pollution
applications.justification: The paper addresses how air pollution affects brain regions structurally and functionally, contributing to psychopathology understanding.
applications.quote: Air pollution was consistently associated with altered structure/function (e.g., increased markers of inflammation, cell death) within the hippocampus...

new_primary_category.justification: The existing category of 'Pollution' adequately describes the paper's focus.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The existing sub-category of 'Air Pollution' adequately covers the paper's theme and focus.
